about: Feature 112 (FR-013, FR-016, FR-018). Every rule that still reports above zero
after this feature's fixes, with the count it reports, who owns paying it down,
and how. A rule absent from this file is enforced at zero: the lint run fails on
any error-severity finding it does not find here.
Counts are per tree because scripts/lint.mjs lints one tree per invocation and
compares against the count for that tree. A single repo-wide total would let a
rise in src hide behind a fall in webview-ui.
The comparison fails in BOTH directions. Above the record is a regression.
Below it is a stale record, which would let the next regression hide behind
today's fix, so a count that falls must be written down here in the same change.
An owner here is a decision, not a person: a quoted heading a reader can grep
plus a path the gate resolves on disk. FR-R3-027 learned that a reference to
'plan.md lines 26 and 66' rots the moment the file is edited, and a name rots
the moment its holder moves on. tests/lint/eslint-baseline.test.ts requires both
halves and both are required by the interface it assigns this file to, so an
unowned entry fails npm run typecheck:tests rather than a gate at run time.

owner.decision: D9 — Six baseline entries, each owned

@typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-condit.reductionNote: 620 checks against values the compiler already types as non-nullable. Most are not dead code; they are the cost of noUncheckedIndexedAccess being off, which types an indexed read as T and so makes the guard after it read as unnecessary. Turning that flag on measures 1,176 errors (verdict in docs/development/lint-and-type-aware-rules.md), so this count falls with that flag, not by editing 620 sites. Lower it opportunistically when a file is already being changed; do not open a sweep.

owner.decision: D9 — Six baseline entries, each owned

@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars.reductionNote: 12 bindings nothing reads, of four kinds: 2 caught-error parameters (src/controller/phase-runner.ts:401, tests/integration/task-lifecycle-events.test.ts:148), 3 unused type imports, 2 dead imports in webview-ui/src/components/PhaseProgression.svelte, and 5 unused destructurings and test-callback parameters. Each is a one-line deletion or an _ prefix with no behavioural risk, so the route is to clear each when its file is next edited. The rule stays at warn per FR-028 and is baselined anyway, because a warn nothing bounds is how 12 becomes 120.

owner.decision: D9 — Six baseline entries, each owned

svelte/prefer-svelte-reactivity.reductionNote: 11 plain Map, Set or Date instances held in reactive state. The fix is the SvelteMap/SvelteSet/SvelteDate equivalents from svelte/reactivity, which changes what re-renders — mutating a plain Map in $state updates nothing today, and will update the DOM afterwards. One commit per component, with that component's tests re-read rather than re-run blind. The rule sits at warn only because a live entry here plus error is the contradiction the FR-017 gate exists to catch; promote it back to error in the same change that clears the count and deletes this entry.

owner.decision: D9 — Six baseline entries, each owned

svelte/require-each-key.reductionNote: 10 keyless {#each} blocks. A key changes how Svelte reuses DOM nodes across a list update: it fixes state leaking between rows when the list reorders, and it can also change which element keeps focus and which transitions play. So each site is a behavioural fix owned by its list's own component, not a mechanical edit. Same promote-to-error procedure as svelte/prefer-svelte-reactivity.

owner.decision: D9 — Six baseline entries, each owned

svelte/prefer-writable-derived.reductionNote: One $state that mirrors a $derived and is written back to. The fix is a writable $derived, which changes when the value resets relative to its source. A single site, so this entry should be the first of the three Svelte entries to reach zero and be deleted.

owner.decision: D10 — Suppression hygiene is a deletion, not a baseline

suppressionDirectives.reductionNote: Four line-scoped eslint-disable comments repo-wide, down from 70; the other 66 named rules that were off or removed and were deleted rather than recorded here. This total is bounded so that lowering a rule count above by suppressing a site shows up as a rise here instead of as an improvement. Of the four: prefer-const at tests/integration/cascaded-pause.test.ts:110 goes when that closure stops needing its binding declared upfront; no-require-imports at tests/integration/index.ts:17 goes when the VS Code test loader takes ESM; the two no-control-regex ones (webview-ui/src/lib/ansi.ts:5 and .../pipeline-catalog-state.ts:465) are load-bearing, because parsing ANSI means matching control characters, and are expected to stay. This count has no tree key, so the lint run skips it and tests/lint/eslint-baseline.test.ts checks it (FR-018).
